actions.reason: C0001 has a coherent RNA-defined biological identity with strong downregulation of metabolic and secretory pathways (22 significant pathways, large negative SMDs, q<0.001). WXS and CNV provide weak, non-significant trends but do not actively contradict the RNA signal. Measured technical factors do not provide a dominant set-specific explanation (no significant set-specific confounders). Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining C0001 as a discovery-stage candidate is better supported than Drop.

C0002 has a coherent CNV-defined biological identity with significant continuous copy-number losses across multiple chromosomal regions (q<0.05). RNA and WXS provide weaker but directionally consistent support (e.g., PBRM1 enrichment, modest pathway upregulation). Measured technical factors do not provide a dominant set-specific explanation (no significant set-specific confounders). Structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining C0002 as a discovery-stage candidate is better supported than Drop.

C0003 lacks a coherent biological identity: RNA shows only one significant pathway, WXS shows no significant enrichment, and CNV shows no significant q-values. The rare CNV events (chr1q loss, chr17p loss) have very wide CIs and are not statistically robust. Cross-modal consistency is weak, with some patients having zero support. No measured technical confounder explains the lack of signal, but the absence of positive identity evidence across all modalities makes retention indefensible. Drop is better supported than Accept, Split, or Merge.

The biological evidence is absent, and the CT-driven identity is confounded. Drop is better supported than Accept, Split, or Merge.
